sections.title: FUM Economics
sections.subtitle: FY2026 introduced seed-capital and performance-fee disclosures; only Operating Cash Flow ex-Seed and Net Seed Investment Flow have a multi-year run (FY2016-FY2026, 22 periods) -- other FUM-flow and mix metrics are FY2026-only and shown as stat cards above rather than charted.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow ex-Seed vs Net Seed Investment Flow
charts.annotation: Statutory operating cash flow (chart above) swung from -A$145m (FY2025) to +A$348m (FY2026) almost entirely on seed-fund subscriptions and redemptions; this pair isolates the core management-fee cash generation from that seed-capital noise.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfExSeed.title: Operating cash flow ex-seed vs net seed investment flow
ocfExSeed.content:
Pinnacle seeds new affiliate funds with its own balance-sheet capital to establish a track record, then redeems that seed as external investors come in. Operating cash flow ex-seed strips those subscriptions/redemptions out of statutory operating cash flow, leaving the cash generated by management and performance fees. Net seed investment flow is the seed capital deployed (negative) or returned (positive) in the period.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: statutory operating cash flow swung from -A$145.2m in FY2025 to +A$348.3m in FY2026 -- almost entirely the seed line (-A$260.8m then +A$235.3m), not the affiliate fee business, which was a steadier ~A$113m ex-seed in FY2026. Reading the statutory OCF number alone materially misjudges the underlying earnings quality in either direction.

What to watch:

  • Ex-seed operating cash flow tracking underlying NPAT over multiple years
  • Large negative seed flows funding a new affiliate or strategy launch (an investment, not a cash cost)
  • Large positive seed flows as funds mature and attract external capital, which is the point of the model working

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Pinnacle Investment Management Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
